Shera says that Amelia has gone missing, but as they’re talking, they receive a report that she was seen boarding a ship bound for Olderion. They make for Olderion to look for her with Shera in tow.

Upon finding her, Shera tries to get her to return to the castle, but Amelia refuses, warning that she will kill him this time if he follows her again. After Amelia leaves, Shera explains that she was initially an assassin sent to kill him, but she abandoned her mission, and Shera has sheltered her ever since.

text.jp:
アメリアの手配書が貼りだされているのを発見したレイン。
シエラに手配書を見せるため城へ向かう。

シエラに会うと、アメリアの行方が分からなくなったと言われる。
そこにアメリアがオルデリオン行きの船に乗ったという報告が入る。シエラも同行し、オルデリオンへとアメリアを探しに行く。

アメリアを見つけた一行。
シエラが城に戻るよう促すも、アメリアはそれを拒否。
追ってくるなら「今度こそ殺す」と物騒な言葉を残し去っていく。

シエラがアメリアの身の上を話す。
彼女は、かつてシエラを暗殺に来た刺客であった。
だが、アメリアはその任務を放棄し、それ以来、シエラは彼女を匿っているのだと……。

だが、任務の放棄は組織においては重罪であった。
アメリアは、組織に帰れば脱走したことは不問になると聞き、組織に戻ることを決めていた。

かつて任務を放棄したのは、ゾルダード生まれの彼女にとって、シエラが救いの光だったからだという。
組織に帰るというアメリアに、説得を試みるシエラ。

……その優しい言葉を受けて、アメリアは、いつになく感情を高ぶらせ、忠誠を誓ってきたシエラに銃を向けた。

組織に戻らなければシエラに危害が及ぶ。
だから、ここでシエラを撃ってでも、シエラを守るために、決別しなければならないのだと、彼女は覚悟を見せた。

だが、シエラはアメリアの脅しを受けてもなお、彼女に寄り添う。
……アメリアの銃口が火を吹くことは、ついぞなかった。

エルフは７００年前の厄災で人間とドワーフに助けられた感謝のため、ディルナド大陸に山を生み出した。
またエルフの存在を後世に伝えるため、最後に男女二人のエルフだけが残ったという。

その二人こそが、フレイヴィアの両親だった。
text.official_en:
In Gaberada, Rain meets an elf who introduces herself as Fryevia. When Rain shows her the elven note he found with Silvia, Fryevia says it reveals that some elves went to Mysidia. She wants to know more about what became of these elves, so together with Rain, they make for the village of Sunioo in Mysidia.

There is a message from the elves there that speaks of their gratitude to humans and dwarves for saving them seven centuries ago, and says that they created mountains in Dirnado to thank their newfound friends. It also says that two elves remained—a man and a woman—to ensure the legacy of the elves was not forgotten. Those two elves were Fryevia’s parents.

They find traces of the elves in Sunioo Village. Out of gratitude to the humans and dwarves who saved them during the calamity seven hundred years ago, the elves created mountains on the continent of Dirnado. It also says that two elves remained—a man and a woman—to ensure the legacy of the elves was not forgotten. Those two elves were Fryevia’s parents.

text.jp:
グランシェルト所属の学者のクロエは、王の依頼でクリスタルについて調査をしていた。
クリスタルの分布の法則性については、未だ解明されていない。
その法則性を調べるために、クリスタル埋蔵量の多いコロボス大陸の地層を調べているという。

レインが採取してきた地層を調べると、ある時点より深い地層にはクリスタルが存在しないことが判明する。
クロエは、かつてのグランシェルトにはクリスタルはなかったのでは、という仮説を立てる。
地層とは、星だけが知る過去を解き明かすための資料である。
伝承で「彼の国の大地は、空にあった」と言われる「天の国」について調べると、クロエは意気込むのだった。
text.official_en:
Chloe, a scholar working for Grandshelt, is investigating crystals at the king’s request.

The geological distribution of crystals is not yet understood. To shed light on this mystery, Chloe is surveying the strata of Kolobos, a continent particularly rich in crystals.

From the samples Rain brought, it becomes clear that crystals are not present in the strata beyond a certain depth.

Chloe theorizes that crystals did not originally exist in Grandshelt.

The geologic strata provide a glimpse into the past known only to the planet itself, and Chloe is enthused to look further into Welkinlond, a country “above cloud and rain” told of in legend.

The sword asks Rain to take it to its other half, apparently somewhere west of Gronoa.

折れた半身はゴロノアの西の方にあるようだ。

襲われる。
撃破したレインは、「折れた刀身」を手に入れることができた。あとは剣の持ち主にこれを届けるだけだ。

Sakura and Roselia spent a lot of time together and grew close. Eventually Roselia left this world, but not before casting one last spell. Sakura couldn’t come to terms with Roselia’s death and subsequently distanced herself from the people of Mysidia.

Back in the present, Sakura finds Roselia’s favorite flower, called a “Mysidia,” and resolves to visit her grave.

Just as Sakura lays the flowers down, Roselia’s staff shines. Perhaps Roselia’s final magic spell has been protecting Sakura and Mysidia all along. The children call out to Sakura, their voices full of hope and cheer. As Sakura bids farewell to Roselia, she is no longer bound by regret. After all, Roselia’s beloved Mysidia still blooms proudly today.

It turns out the people were talking about Aileen, the rebels’ weaponsmith. Rain asks her to make weapons for him and his friends, but she says she’ll only do it if he answers her questions in a satisfactory manner.

Rain and the others decide to learn more about Aileen in order to prepare to answer the questions. They discover that she’s really passionate about weapon-making and return feeling fully ready to answer anything she might ask them.

Rain answers her questions with true sincerity, so Aileen agrees to make weapons for them. She says that life has become much easier and that there’s greater efficiency on the battlefield and in the weapons people use. But this means people might forget the weight of the lives they’re taking, even though soldiers and weapon-makers are supposed to be fighting for a more peaceful future. She can’t accept this fallacy, so she does her best to fight against the times. She clings to her ideals, even if it seems like she’s just blowing smoke. Rain and the others also strive to create a world where they can express their ideals proudly, and so Aileen decides to board their ship.

アメリアは「そろそろ返事がほしい」というシエラの言葉を伝えると、立ち去っていった。

アメリアの言葉を聞いたジェイクは、スラムで確認したいことが
あると言う。

かつて病床のジェイクの母親をソゼ皇帝がどこかへ連れだした。
そして、帰ってきた時、幸せそうにしていたのだと。
ジェイクは、二人が出かけた場所がケリス駅だという情報を
手に入れた。

……ジェイクの母親は平民の出だった。
城の給仕係だった彼女は、ソゼ皇帝と恋に落ちた。
だが、二人は身分違いであり、その仲は引き裂かれた。だが、その頃には、彼女は既にジェイクを身ごもっていた。
どんな事情があれど、母を捨てたソゼを許せないジェイクだったが、
病床の母親を看病をする姿に、自分には気づかない何かが二人の間にあると感じた。

Their relationship fell apart due to their differences in status, even though she was already pregnant. Jake always hated Sozhe for tossing his mother aside, but when the emperor came to tend to his mother when she was sick, he sensed something between them.

Rumors are spreading throughout Zoldaad about a phantom train which runs through an old station that was abandoned years ago after a terrible accident. Because there are multiple witness accounts, Rain decides to investigate.

Upon arriving at the abandoned station, Rain is beset by a sudden drowsiness. When he wakes up, he finds himself inside the phantom train and meets a mercenary named Camille who is also there to investigate the train. They decide to work together.

Rain and Camille question the train’s passengers—the victims of the accident. It turns out a number of them were under the command of General Wilhelm, who was executed for staging a rebellion against Emperor Sozhe. The soldiers were to deliver a report from General Wilhelm to Prince Shera.

Camille picks up a mysterious note that’s written in some kind of code.

After questioning some more passengers, they discover that Lazarov had discerned General Wilhelm’s plan and destroyed the train in a way that made it look like an accident. Camille says the phantom train was created by a monster that feeds off the regrets of the dead, and to defeat this monster, Rain has to confront them with the reason why the train is still running.

Rain and Camille find the passenger the monster is disguised as, and Rain confronts them, saying the reason the train is still running is because of the soldiers’ regrets over not being able to save Zoldaad. After they successfully defeat the phantom train, Rain tells the soldiers’ spirits that he and his friends personally put an end to Lazarov, then he falls asleep again.

When he wakes up, he’s back in Mozul Station. Camille, who had also safely escaped the train, decides to tag along on the airship.

Further questioning reveals that Lazarov noticed Wilhelm’s movements and destroyed the train while making it look like an accident. Camille recognizes the work of a monster she knows, one that exploits the regrets of the dead to keep the phantom train running. To defeat it, they must confront it with the reason the train continues to run.

Rumors are spreading throughout Zoldaad about a phantom train which runs through an old station that was abandoned years ago after a terrible accident. Because there are multiple witness accounts, Rain decides to investigate.

Upon arriving at the abandoned station, Rain is beset by a sudden drowsiness. When he wakes up, he finds himself inside the phantom train and meets a mercenary named Camille who is also there to investigate the train. They decide to work together.

Rain and Camille question the train’s passengers—the victims of the accident. It turns out a number of them were under the command of General Wilhelm, who was executed for staging a rebellion against Emperor Sozhe. The soldiers were to deliver a report from General Wilhelm to Prince Shera.

Camille picks up a mysterious note that’s written in some kind of code.

After questioning some more passengers, they discover that Lazarov had discerned General Wilhelm’s plan and destroyed the train in a way that made it look like an accident. Camille says the phantom train was created by a monster that feeds off the regrets of the dead, and to defeat this monster, Rain has to confront them with the reason why the train is still running.

The train has passengers. Everyone they question appears to have died in the accident, including soldiers who served General Wilhelm, who was executed after turning against Emperor Sozhe. The soldiers had been trying to deliver some kind of report from Wilhelm to Crown Prince Shera.

Camille finds a mysterious note, but it is written in a code they cannot read.

Further questioning reveals that Lazarov noticed Wilhelm’s movements and destroyed the train while making it look like an accident. Camille recognizes the work of a monster she knows, one that exploits the regrets of the dead to keep the phantom train running. To defeat it, they must confront it with the reason the train continues to run.

Rain goes to the Earth Shrine to retrieve a banner he and Scott designed when founding the squadron, hoping to rekindle Scott’s passion, but the cause of Scott’s despondency is that his eyesight is fading due to illness.

Rain gives Scott Dew of Reprieve—something that may slow the progress of his condition—and asks the engineer to direct the squadron’s reconstruction, telling him that even with failing eyesight, his experience is enough to make it happen.

Scott calls Rain an idealist, but then recalls Rain’s belief in making ideals into reality.

Rain leaves the decision in Scott’s hands and departs, holding fast to his ideals.
